notes:
The first release. The Foundry interface becomes the device your character wears, and its switch raises the character sheet as a projection over the canvas. Every roll and button is still the game system's own.

Highlights

  • Seven devices: the omni-tool, wrist computer, EVA (GDI and Nod) and TRON for science fiction; the Adventurer's Journal and the Runic Vambrace for fantasy.
  • Eleven looks over them, from a flickering hologram and an old green terminal to a stone Runeforge and a Journal bound in green leather.
  • The projection: vitals, defenses, effects, a readout and tabbed pages, with hit points, experience, conditions, spells, inventory and the biography changed in place.
  • PF2e, SF2e and D&D 5e, each through the system's own calls.
  • The whole interface in the device's colors: sidebar, chat, a scene bar with previews, controls, the player list, and an optional carousel turn order.
  • A Mass Effect dossier with the conversion's shields and Paragon/Renegade.

Everything in 1.0.0

Rebuilt as a UI theme. The HUD is no longer a character sheet; the interface itself is the device, and the character sheet is a projection it raises over the canvas.

  • The device at the foot of the screen, with Foundry's own macro bar mounted on it: the omni-tool's forearm and emitter band, or a docked bar with a power key for the others.
  • The projection: identity, vitals, defenses, effects, readout and a tabbed main panel, built to the approved mock-up for each device and scaled to the room the interface leaves.
  • PF2e, SF2e and D&D 5e, through adapters that hand every button to the system's own API.

Full details in the release notes.
